The ambition is real, but the spending profile is what investors are pricing, and Bloomberg reported Gelsinger is tired of Wall Street doubting his comeback plan [[n1101]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

Intel closed at 45.04 USD, -5.32% on the session and -13.45% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), and Tom's Hardware reported AMD's market cap surpassing Intel's for the first time [[n0381]]. Until the spending shows returns, the stock lacks a floor. Risk to the bear case: the $5.4 billion Tower Semiconductor acquisition, announced by Intel [[n0454]], could revalue its foundry ambitions.
Trade Expression
Underweight Intel against AMD within semiconductors; cover if Intel reclaims its 20-session reference of 52.04 USD.

catalysts.title: Nvidia (NVDA)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

AlphaStreet published a snapshot of Nvidia's fourth-quarter fiscal 2022 earnings [[n1133]], a print Barron's had framed as a big day for the metaverse after Roblox [[n0590]], and Al Jazeera reported an upbeat current-quarter revenue forecast [[n1821]]. Techcircle reported the FTC saying the end of the Arm acquisition attempt bodes well for competition [[n1833]], which removes a regulatory overhang but also a growth option.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Nvidia closed at 236.42 USD, -3.53% on the session and +1.15% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18): the beat has not lifted the stock out of its rate-driven range. Risk: higher real yields compress the multiple regardless of revenue momentum.
Trade Expression
Hold core exposure but add only if Nvidia outperforms SOXX after the holiday; cut if it breaks its 20-session reference of 233.74 USD.

catalysts.title: Walmart (WMT)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Walmart is the clearest scale beneficiary of food inflation: the WSJ reported it withstanding pandemic blows and higher costs to boost business [[n1147]], and Al Jazeera reported it thriving despite supply-chain woes and high inflation [[n0816]]. Grocery share gains make price increases easier to pass through.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Walmart closed at 137.99 USD, +1.97% over five sessions but -1.57% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18); the hurdle is its 20-session reference of 140.19 USD. Risk: CNBC reported shoppers on alert as grocery bills climb [[n0818]], so trade-down could pressure margins if wage growth fades.
Trade Expression
Overweight Walmart against discretionary retail as the staples leg of the pricing-power trade; reassess if management commentary points to falling volumes.

catalysts.title: Alibaba (BABA)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

The BBC reported Alibaba and Tencent sites added to the US 'Notorious Markets List' [[n0254]], and Barron's reported the same counterfeit and piracy designation [[n0253]], in the same week Bloomberg reported Beijing's new fee policy wiping $26 billion off Meituan's value [[n0848]]. Caixin reported Hillhouse ditching Alibaba while buying NEV makers [[n0480]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

Alibaba's US ADR closed at 118.99 USD, -4.37% on the session, and the Hong Kong line at 119.50 HKD, -2.85% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The hurdle is the ADR's 20-session reference of 123.23 USD. Risk: a policy pivot pairing PBOC easing with regulatory relief could squeeze shorts.
Trade Expression
Hold BABA underweight as the short leg against ASHR; cover if the ADR reclaims 123.23 USD on a policy-easing signal.

catalysts.title: Airbus (AIR.PA)
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Statista reported Airbus soaring back out of the red [[n1843]], and AirGuide reported a record $4.8 billion net income pulling it away from Boeing [[n1844]]. Reuters reported Airbus finalising the sale of seven A350 freighters to Singapore Airlines [[n0387]], while US regulators are inspecting new Boeing 787s, per Reuters [[n0517]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

Airbus closed at 115.00 EUR, -2.95% over five sessions and +1.41% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The WSJ reported its plan to ramp up production of its bestselling jet hitting snags [[n0695]], and Reuters reported Airbus reviewing its defence business as pressures mount [[n0578]]. Risk: the Seattle Times reported Airbus workers authorising a strike over pay at UK wing plants [[n1793]].
Trade Expression
Overweight Airbus against Boeing as the cleaner commercial-aerospace exposure; reassess if ramp snags force a cut to delivery targets.

spec.retail_intro: Retail heads into Presidents' Day holding stock bets it cannot trade until Tuesday, led by a Truth Social launch set for the holiday itself: a classic buy-the-rumour setup, in which the crowd prices a public date in advance and the event decides whether the first gap pays early holders or traps late ones.

retail.title: Digital World Acquisition / DWAC — Truth Social's launch is set for a holiday
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The story the DWAC crowd tells itself fits on a bumper sticker: Trump's app is due in the App Store on Presidents' Day, and the ticker tied to his media company reprices the moment trading reopens. Digital World Acquisition, the SPAC for Trump Media & Technology Group, closed at 84.32 USD, up 15.32% from 73.12 USD on January 21 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The pull is a lottery ticket with a cause attached, a wager on what Vanity Fair calls Trump's attempt at a Twitter competitor [[n1744]]. The holiday sharpens the itch: the catalyst is set for a day when US exchanges are shut, so holders will watch the event they bet on without being able to trade it, and the date is so public it feels like a sure thing.
What Is Driving It

Reuters reported, citing an executive, that Truth Social is set for release on Monday in Apple's App Store [[n0932]]; Axios [[n1766]] and Slate [[n1763]] carried the same Presidents' Day debut, after Reuters said the app had opened to hundreds of testers [[n1742]]. The fine print is duller: Nunes said the app will be fully operational by the end of March, according to The Guardian [[n1765]], so Monday is a front door rather than a finished building. The tape is hostile: the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.14% to 14,009.54 index points on February 18, the VIX closed at 27.75 index points and Robinhood Markets dropped 11.34% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). DWAC slipped 1.37% on Friday but kept a 2.83% five-session gain, a stock trading on its own calendar.
The Social Signal

Attention is abundant, and its shape is the tell. The Guardian took readers inside the beta as testers got a glimpse of the app [[n1752]], Vanity Fair told them to get ready for Retruths [[n1744]], and Snopes found it worth fact-checking whether the app will cost users $4.99 a week [[n1755]], the kind of claim that only gets checked once it is travelling. None of that counts buyers, but a stock whose catalyst is a consumer app lives on mainstream curiosity: everyone who learns the date is a potential download and, for some, a DWAC order. The coverage fixes the date in every holder's mind, which crowds the reaction into a single session.
Historical Analog

The sharpest analog is days old. Virgin Galactic surged 30% after the company announced $450,000 tickets to space, Forbes reported [[n0523]]; by Friday CNBC reported that Chamath Palihapitiya, who took the company public, had stepped down from its board [[n0844]], a resignation Forbes set against a stock crash [[n0903]]. SPCE closed at 8.40 USD, down 6.77% on the day and 0.47% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18): the pop round-tripped inside a week. The mechanics map onto DWAC: a dated consumer event, a SPAC wrapper, a famous sponsor and a crowd buying the date rather than the economics. In spikes like these the event tends to be the exit for early holders, not the entry for latecomers, because every rumour buyer watches the same calendar.
Smart Money View

Professional opinion splits over the business, not the ticker. The New York Times says Truth Social is poised to join a crowded field [[n1767]], while the chief executives of Parler and Gettr welcomed Trump's platform, Bloomberg reported [[n1730]], a sign the audience is real but contested. Above the stock, professionals are positioning for trouble, not a lottery win: Bloomberg reported a big options trade hedging an S&P 500 plunge of up to 20% by April [[n2043]], and Wolf Street says margin debt plunged as high-fliers got crushed, yet leverage is still gigantic [[n1310]]. Professionals will judge monetisation over quarters; the crowd will likely judge the launch by its first days in the App Store.
When the Narrative Breaks

The first test is Tuesday's open. DWAC has not traded since its 84.32 USD close on February 18, so whatever Monday's launch delivers, and a weekend in which the BBC reported Biden is convinced Putin has decided to invade [[n1424]], arrive in one gap. The bulls' line is the 73.12 USD close of January 21 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18): a break below it would erase the whole 15.32% run into the launch and stamp this a sell-the-news event. The second test is Nunes's own end-of-March timetable [[n1765]]: a phased rollout that leaves would-be users waiting is the anticlimax that turns a lottery ticket into a bag. And a blank-check shell priced on the Trump Media deal story, not on Truth Social revenue, can gap on headlines unrelated to downloads.

retail.title: Bitcoin / BTC-USD — the dip-buyers meet Buterin's winter
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Crypto was retail's only open market all weekend, and it voted early: Bitcoin closed at 38,431.38 USD, down 4.21% on the day and 13.78% over five sessions, while Ether fell 17.33% over the same five sessions to 2,628.65 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-20). The crowd's reflex is to buy the dip, and it has a head of state as mascot: Business Insider Africa calls El Salvador's Nayib Bukele a president for the meme-stock generation, obsessed with stonks, silly numbers, bitcoin and the dip [[n1762]]. The awkward voice comes from inside the house: Ethereum founder Buterin says crypto welcomes another winter, Bloomberg reports [[n1001]].
Where It Breaks

A winter is not a dip. Bitcoin's 20-session change has slipped to -0.13%, leaving it just below its January 31 close of 38,483.12 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-20). The newest holders, recruited by a Super Bowl blitz whose audience ADWEEK is still questioning [[n0995]], are likely the least patient. Marathon Digital, at 23.89 USD, and Coinbase, at 189.16 USD, last traded before the weekend slide (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), so Tuesday's open is a gap to absorb; if they reprice lower and Bitcoin cannot reclaim 38,483.12 USD, the dip becomes the trend.

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — Musk picks a fight with the SEC
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Tesla's retail base does not just own a stock; it backs a protagonist, and the protagonist is in a fight. Musk and Tesla attacked the SEC for unrelenting harassment, Reuters reports [[n0736]], and Forbes describes the charge of a calculated effort to chill his free speech [[n1851]]. For the faithful that is a rallying cry, and the old enemy is back: Teslarati reports a longtime short-seller betting against the stock again despite low short interest [[n1711]]. Tesla closed at 856.98 USD, down 2.21% on February 18 and 9.21% over 20 sessions from 943.90 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), which believers read as a cheaper ticket to the same story.
Where It Breaks

The regulator fight now has a product edge. Reuters reports a US investigation of 416,000 Tesla vehicles over unexpected braking [[n1867]], and Time warns that Tesla's latest scandals could hurt its bottom line [[n1834]]. Loyalty is not a valuation, and a stock priced on its founder's credibility pays first when the headlines move from free speech to safety. The faith breaks if Tesla keeps failing below the 943.90 USD of January 21 while the braking probe stays in the news.

retail.title: Gold Miners ETF / GDX — the war hedge waits for Tuesday
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The invasion hedge is back for another round. Gold futures closed at 1,899.80 USD/oz, up 3.13% over five sessions, and the GDX miners rose 6.38% to 34.50 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The weekend raised the stakes: the BBC reported Biden is convinced Putin has decided to invade [[n1424]], Reuters that Putin would oversee nuclear drills [[n1422]], and on Sunday Axios reported Russia extended drills in Belarus [[n1435]], news US-listed miners have yet to trade. GLD even made Yahoo Finance's list of top trades for Tuesday [[n0834]].
Where It Breaks

The haven is a bet on escalation, so any diplomatic opening drains the fear premium, and geared miners give it back fastest. Rates are the slower threat, the subject of a Visual Capitalist explainer on how interest-rate hikes affect gold's price [[n1776]]. A GDX slide back toward its January 21 close of 31.65 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) would say the war premium has gone.
